topic: Revive parent exp_platform_ncc_drift_minimax_frontier with a phase-correct all-kernel comparison rather than its refuted all-positive-floor claim. In the unchanged bounded finite-population adaptive platform model, prove that the optimized clipped predictable-AIPW radius R* and unrestricted uniformly honest variable-length minimax expected length L* are uniformly comparable iff the common available-arm floor p_floor exceeds alpha. For p_floor>alpha, establish M(p_floor-alpha)s <= L* <= 2R* <= [8 sqrt((1-p_floor)/(alpha p_floor))/(p_floor-alpha)]L*, s^2=sum_{b in W}q_b^2/n_b, under arbitrary outcome-adaptive propensities. For p_floor<=alpha, prove no finite uniform comparison and solve the one-window-unit boundary exactly. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A product-uniform prior on focal potential outcomes with all controls zero stays in every TV budget pathwise. Conditional on the actual adaptive record, unseen focal coordinates remain independent uniforms. A weighted-uniform density lemma and missing squared-weight mass Q yield E(Qc)>=(p_floor-alpha)s^2 and hence L*>=M(p_floor-alpha)s. Concurrent weights give the displayed upper constant. The continuous one-unit experiment has L*=2M[p_floor-alpha]_+ and R*=2M above the boundary, proving sharp 1/(p_floor-alpha) blow-up. In the nonadaptive one-unit three-block family, L*=(1-alpha)D+(2M-D)[p_floor-alpha]_+, D=min(Gamma,2M), so strict all-kernel NCC gain holds iff Gamma<2M. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently audit the posterior factorization, density lemma, and inherited radius constants; obtain an intrinsic strict-NCC-gain criterion for general continuous outcome-adaptive designs or state its impossibility boundary without substituting an AIPW KKT result. EARLY KILL TEST: Reconstruct the one-unit continuum proof, then condition the product prior through an outcome-adaptive two-unit assignment tree and verify that no missing focal coordinate enters the record likelihood; any failure, or any compatible design violating the Q coverage-budget inequality, kills the positive theorem. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_platform_ncc_floorphase_minimax_frontier.md

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether p_floor > alpha is exactly the condition under which the optimized clipped predictable-AIPW radius is uniformly comparable to unrestricted uniformly honest variable-length minimax expected length in bounded finite-population adaptive platform experiments.

source_refs.excerpt: For each fixed p_floor in (0,1/2], prove or refute the existence of a finite comparison constant.
The fixed-floor converse is false as stated.

source_refs.claim: Predictable reweighting stabilizes AIPW inference under adaptive assignment, but is not compared with unrestricted finite-sample minimax expected length.
source_refs.author: Hadad, Hirshberg, Zhan, Wager, and Athey
source_refs.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

source_refs.claim: Design-based intervals are constructed for finite-population means under adaptive bandit assignment, without an all-procedure expected-length benchmark or coverage-level positivity threshold.
source_refs.author: Ham, Bojinov, Lindon, and Tingley

source_refs.claim: Bayes-minimax duality characterizes minimax expected-measure confidence sets in fixed experiments, not response-adaptive missing-potential-outcome experiments.
source_refs.author: Evans, Hansen, and Stark

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent established that experiment-specific positivity alone is insufficient but grouped all fixed common floors into one unresolved subclass. Adaptive-inference papers control particular IPW or AIPW procedures through predictable weighting, clipping, martingale limits, or concentration; minimax-confidence-set papers optimize expected length in fixed experiments. Neither literature compares a clipped AIPW radius with every measurable honest variable-length interval when adaptive assignment reveals only one potential outcome per unit. The proposed boundary is instead a coverage-budget phenomenon: an event of probability at most alpha may be sacrificed entirely. Above the boundary, the missing argument is a product-prior lower bound surviving arbitrary outcome feedback, plus an independent audit of the inherited radius constants.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A verified phase theorem proving M(p_floor-alpha)s <= L* <= 2R* <= [8 sqrt((1-p_floor)/(alpha p_floor))/(p_floor-alpha)]L* for p_floor>alpha, proving that no finite uniform comparison exists for p_floor<=alpha, and deriving the exact one-window-unit values L*=2M[p_floor-alpha]_+ and R*=2M above the boundary.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves from the operational value of adaptive allocation to inverse-propensity instability and predictable AIPW stabilization; the destination can retain that arc while replacing asymptotic validity with an all-kernel finite-population benchmark.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive allocation improves learning or participant welfare -> declining assignment probabilities destabilize ordinary IPW inference -> predictable AIPW weights restore usable intervals -> determine exactly when those intervals are uniformly competitive with unrestricted honest procedures

method_exemplars.technique: Use test inversion and Bayes-minimax duality to lower-bound worst-case expected interval length through a least-favorable prior.
method_exemplars.why_closest: L* is an unrestricted minimax expected-length value, with the adaptive assignment record replacing the paper's fixed statistical experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Condition on fixed potential outcomes and use predictable assignment probabilities with martingale concentration to construct design-based intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its randomness source and finite-population estimands match the destination; the new proof must add an all-procedure lower bound and optimized clipping comparison.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize worst-case bias plus stochastic radius and compare the resulting interval with honest-procedure efficiency bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired theorem likewise joins a bias-aware optimized radius to unrestricted honest expected length, but under adaptive randomization rather than a Gaussian likelihood.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize when conditioning a product-uniform prior on the realized outcome-adaptive assignment record preserves the independence and uniformity of every unrevealed focal potential outcome, and whether this yields the sharp missing-squared-weight-mass coverage inequality.

source_refs.claim: Selective randomization inference conditions on information driving adaptive decisions, but does not establish least-favorable-prior posterior factorization for arbitrary bounded potential outcomes.
source_refs.author: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao
source_refs.venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B

source_refs.claim: Finite-population IPW and AIPW theory is developed for general adaptive designs, but its asymptotic guarantees do not supply the required posterior-product lower-bound argument.
source_refs.author: Li and Zhao

source_refs.claim: Design-based bandit inference conditions on the finite population and known adaptive randomization, leaving the Bayesian change-of-measure law of unseen coordinates untreated.
source_refs.author: Ham, Bojinov, Lindon, and Tingley

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent's deterministic masking proof identifies histories on which selected schedules induce the same observations, but the proposed product prior requires more: conditional on the entire adaptive record, the record likelihood must not involve any unrevealed coordinate even though revealed focal outcomes may change later propensities. Existing design-based analyses condition on potential outcomes rather than placing a prior on them, while selective-randomization work conditions adaptive decisions to calibrate tests rather than to prove a minimax Bayes bound. The first fragile step is the sequential path-likelihood factorization; the second is a weighted-uniform density lemma converting conditional coverage into E(Qc)>=(p_floor-alpha)s^2. A two-unit outcome-adaptive tree is the minimal audit capable of exposing posterior leakage or a failure of the coverage-budget inequality.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A filtration-level posterior-factorization lemma, a weighted-uniform coverage lemma implying E(Qc)>=(p_floor-alpha)s^2, and either a proof that both hold for every compatible outcome-adaptive assignment tree or an explicit two-unit counterexample identifying the failing likelihood factor.

writing_exemplar.why: Its graphical framing makes the information reused by adaptive decisions explicit and treats conditional validity as the central obstacle.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Interim outcomes alter later experimental decisions -> conditioning on those decisions can leak information -> a filtration analysis isolates what the adaptive mechanism actually observes -> determine exactly when unseen potential outcomes retain their product-prior law

method_exemplars.technique: Represent adaptive recruitment and assignment through a DAG and condition on the sigma-field used by the adaptive decision to establish the valid selective randomization law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The posterior-factorization problem is a conditional-independence question about the same adaptive record, with a least-favorable-prior lower bound replacing selective testing.

method_exemplars.technique: Integrate uniform coverage constraints under a prior and use density bounds to lower-bound expected confidence-set measure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once posterior factorization is verified, this is the closest proof architecture for converting residual prior uncertainty into an all-procedure expected-length bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Factor adaptive assignment laws with history-predictable kernels and represent AIPW errors as finite-population martingale differences.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its filtration conventions are directly suited to testing whether the sequential likelihood depends only on coordinates revealed before each assignment.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize exactly when nonconcurrent controls strictly reduce unrestricted uniformly honest minimax expected interval length relative to concurrent-only inference under continuous outcomes, outcome-adaptive randomization, and bounded temporal drift.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The parent's KKT certificate compares two constructed AIPW objectives, not the optimal observed-data interval kernels of the full and concurrent-only experiments. Existing NCC work likewise studies identification, model-based validity, or semiparametric efficiency for specified estimators. Variable-length kernels can allocate miscoverage unevenly across revealing histories, so an AIPW-radius improvement is not visibly necessary or sufficient for strict all-kernel gain. The missing object is an intrinsic comparison of the observed-data experiments—through common-mass geometry, deficiency, distinguishability, or exact coverage polytopes—that remains valid with continuous outcomes and outcome-dependent assignment.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient observed-law or coverage-polytope criterion for L*_NCC<L*_CC in general continuous adaptive designs, with an attaining construction and a specialization proving L*=(1-alpha)D+(2M-D)[p_floor-alpha]_+ and strict gain iff Gamma<2M in the nonadaptive one-unit three-block family.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames NCC use through the estimand, identifying assumptions, and genuine information gains while clearly separating deterministic and stochastic availability.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Platform arms enter at different times -> earlier controls are attractive but are not concurrently randomized -> availability and drift assumptions govern what those controls add -> characterize when borrowing strictly improves honest minimax precision rather than only a chosen estimator's variance

method_exemplars.technique: Express the concurrent causal estimand under explicit availability mechanisms and compare the efficient influence functions of concurrent-only and pooled-control observed-data models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its deterministic-versus-stochastic availability partition is the nearest existing structural precursor to an intrinsic strict-gain criterion.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive minimax confidence-length lower bounds with least-favorable submodels and construct bias-enlarged oracle intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: NCC borrowing under bounded drift is structurally an auxiliary-data problem with controlled discrepancy, but with adaptive randomization replacing the Gaussian auxiliary experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Bayes-minimax duality over confidence sets without restricting attention to affine or fixed-length procedures.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination compares unrestricted variable-length kernels and therefore needs an all-procedure characterization rather than another estimator optimization.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether one design-based nonconcurrent-control interval can adapt honestly to an unknown total-variation drift budget Gamma with near-oracle expected length under arbitrary outcome-adaptive propensities, or quantify the unavoidable adaptation penalty.

source_refs.excerpt: Add the unknown-drift adaptation question as a separately scoped follow-on theorem or impossibility result.
No claim is made that the drift budget is learned.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The known-Gamma radius selects borrowing weights using a fixed worst-case bias budget. Estimating Gamma from observed controls and reusing it for weight selection can invalidate uniform coverage because target-relevant counterfactual drift remains partly unobserved. The nested TV balls therefore form a between-class adaptation problem under schedule-dependent adaptive assignment laws, while existing Gaussian auxiliary-data results do not compute this randomization-law geometry. The oracle benchmark may also change discontinuously at p_floor=alpha, so a conventional smooth oracle inequality need not be attainable.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a single uniformly honest interval satisfying an explicit oracle expected-length inequality relative to inf_Gamma L*(Gamma), including its behavior at p_floor=alpha, or a between-TV-class modulus lower bound giving the sharp multiplicative or additive adaptation penalty.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing separates the gains available with a known auxiliary-data bias bound from the limits of adapting to an unknown bound.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Auxiliary observations can improve precision when their discrepancy is controlled -> the optimal amount of borrowing depends on the bias radius -> the radius is not identified from the primary randomization -> determine the honest price of adapting across drift budgets

method_exemplars.technique: Use ordered and between-class moduli to compare attainable expected interval lengths over nested parameter spaces under uniform honesty.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The Gamma-indexed bounded-drift schedule classes are nested, making the destination an honest expected-length adaptation problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct oracle intervals under a bounded discrepancy and establish adaptive-confidence-interval lower bounds across unknown discrepancy classes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the analogous auxiliary-data adaptation problem; the first proof component requiring replacement is its fixed likelihood by an adaptive randomization experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Optimize bias-aware confidence intervals over convex nuisance classes and analyze the coverage cost of data-dependent tuning.
method_exemplars.why_closest: An adaptive NCC interval must tune borrowing using the same observations used for inference while retaining worst-case coverage over temporal drift.

literature_map:
Hadad et al. (2021, PNAS, arXiv:1911.02768) explain why ordinary IPW becomes heavy-tailed under adaptive assignment and introduce predictably weighted AIPW for asymptotic coverage.
Cook, Mishler, and Ramdas (2024, AISTATS, arXiv:2311.18274) strengthen adaptive-AIPW limit theory, add confidence sequences, and use propensity truncation for finite-sample stability.
Kato et al. (2020, arXiv:2002.05308) optimize adaptive allocation for ATE efficiency and provide anytime-valid intervals for their selected design.
Armstrong (2022, arXiv:2205.02726) shows that outcome-adaptive assignment cannot improve first-order superpopulation ATE efficiency beyond an optimal nonadaptive propensity design.
Ham et al. (2023, arXiv:2302.14136) give design-based finite-population intervals for nonstationary bandits, but not unrestricted minimax expected-length comparisons.
Ham et al. (2022, arXiv:2210.08639) provide assumption-light design-based confidence sequences, leaving minimax width under platform availability untreated.
Li and Zhao (2026, arXiv:2602.21998) develop finite-population IPW/AIPW theory for general adaptive designs, including vanishing propensities and nonconverging regressions.
Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026, JRSSB, arXiv:2405.07026) use DAG-guided selective randomization inference, highlighting exactly which adaptive information is conditioned upon.
Santacatterina et al. (2025, Statistics in Medicine, arXiv:2404.19118) find no doubly robust NCC efficiency gain under deterministic availability, but possible gain under stochastic availability.
Marschner (2024, Biometrical Journal, DOI:10.1002/bimj.202300334) argues that NCC status is design-defined and that time adjustment alone need not remove the nonrandomized component.
Bofill Roig et al. (2022, BMC Medical Research Methodology, arXiv:2112.06574) obtain power gains from NCC step-trend models under equal additive trends, with type-I-error inflation under misspecification.
Guo, Wang, and Yuan (2024, Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research, DOI:10.1080/19466315.2023.2292238) propose propensity-weighted drift adjustment within a model-based rather than all-kernel minimax analysis.
Chen, Zhang, and Ye (2026 revision, arXiv:2109.10522) show that auxiliary data can shorten minimax intervals under a known bias bound while adaptation to unknown bias is generally impossible.
Evans, Hansen, and Stark (2005, Bernoulli, DOI:10.3150/bj/1126126761) and Armstrong-Kolesar (2018, Econometrica, DOI:10.3982/ECTA14434) provide Bayes-minimax and modulus machinery for honest interval length in fixed experiments.
Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, arXiv:2608.13822) optimize unrestricted finite-population randomized-experiment estimation risk but do not address honest interval length, adaptive assignment, NCC drift, or the p_floor-alpha phase.
